  "description": "Moniepoint is Africa&#39;s all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria&rsquo;s largest merchant acquirer.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

Job Position: Data Entry Officer

Job Locations: Oredo and Ikpoba Okha - Edo
Employment Type: Full-time
Work Mode: Outsourced and Hybrid

Job Purpose


	The Data Entry Specialist ensures that customer accounts, product catalogues, inventory records, and pricing data are accurately entered and maintained within the Moniebook platform.
	Working closely with Onboarding Specialists and Account Managers, you keep data clean and ready from day one, enabling fast go - lives, reliable reporting, and a smooth experience for every retail customer.
	Success is measured by accuracy rates, turnaround time, and your contribution to a scalable, error - free operational foundation.


Key Responsibilities
Data Entry &amp; Record Management:


	Input, update, and maintain merchant data, including product catalogues, SKUs, pricing, inventory levels, and customer profiles.
	Process bulk data imports from spreadsheets and CSV files, validating format and completeness before upload.
	Ensure all records adhere to Moniebook&#39;s data standards and naming conventions.


Onboarding Data Support:


	Prepare merchant accounts ahead of onboarding by populating required product, inventory, and configuration data within agreed timelines.
	Review merchant - submitted data templates for errors or missing fields and follow up to resolve gaps before entry.
	Support the setup of catalogue structures, tax configurations, and payment settings as directed by the Onboarding team.


Data Validation &amp; Quality Assurance:


	Conduct checks to identify and correct errors, duplicates, or outdated records.
	Cross-reference data across spreadsheets, CRM, and POS backend to ensure consistency.
	Flag and document data anomalies, routing them to the appropriate team for resolution.


Process &amp; Documentation:


	Maintain accurate records of data entry activities, import logs, and correction history in the CRM.
	Document common errors and resolutions to build a shared knowledge base and reduce repeat mistakes.
	Identify recurring workflow bottlenecks and recommend improvements to the Operations lead.


Cross-Functional Collaboration:


	Fulfil ad-hoc data requests from Onboarding Specialists, Account Managers, and Support teams within SLA windows.
	Coordinate with internal teams to gather missing customer data without delaying onboarding timelines.


Qualifications


	1 - 3 years in data entry, data operations, or a similar role &mdash; preferably in SaaS, retail tech, or fintech.
	Exceptional attention to detail with a track record of high accuracy across large data volumes.
	Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets (data cleaning, VLOOKUP / XLOOKUP, basic formulas).
	Familiarity with CRM platforms or POS / back-office SaaS tools.
	Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.


Preferred:


	Experience with bulk CSV imports, data migration, or catalogue management in a SaaS context.
	Exposure to retail operations, inventory systems, or point - of - sale platforms.
	Experience supporting an onboarding, implementation, or customer success team.
	The candidate should be based in Edo State - Oredo and Ikpoba Okha.


About You:


	You&#39;re obsessively detail - orientated and take genuine pride in clean, accurate data.
	You&#39;re process - driven but proactive; you follow workflows and flag problems before they escalate.
	You&#39;re a team player who understands that your work sits at the heart of the customer journey.
	You&#39;re calm under pressure and can handle high volumes without cutting corners.
	You&#39;re tech - savvy and always looking for smarter, faster ways to work.


What Success Looks Like:


	99%+ data entry accuracy across merchant account builds and catalogue uploads.
	Zero go - live delays attributable to data readiness.
	All ad-hoc data requests fulfilled within defined SLA windows
	Open task backlog kept below 5% at any given time.
	Achieve &gt;4.5+ average rating score from Onboarding Specialists and Account Managers on data quality and turnaround.


What we can offer you


	Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We&rsquo;ve built a company where all voices are heard, and we look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
	Learning: We have a learning - and development - focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing and training.
	Compensation: You&rsquo;ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, plus other benefits.


What to expect in the hiring process


	A preliminary phone call with the recruiter.
	An interview with the hiring team.
	An interview with a member of our executive team.

Data Entry Officer Job at Moniepoint




        
    

        
        Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

Job Position: Data Entry Officer

Job Locations: Oredo and Ikpoba Okha - Edo
Employment Type: Full-time
Work Mode: Outsourced and Hybrid

Job Purpose
     

            
    




	The Data Entry Specialist ensures that customer accounts, product catalogues, inventory records, and pricing data are accurately entered and maintained within the Moniebook platform.
	Working closely with Onboarding Specialists and Account Managers, you keep data clean and ready from day one, enabling fast go - lives, reliable reporting, and a smooth experience for every retail customer.
	Success is measured by accuracy rates, turnaround time, and your contribution to a scalable, error - free operational foundation.


Key Responsibilities
Data Entry & Record Management:


	Input, update, and maintain merchant data, including product catalogues, SKUs, pricing, inventory levels, and customer profiles.
	Process bulk data imports from spreadsheets and CSV files, validating format and completeness before upload.
	Ensure all records adhere to Moniebook's data standards and naming conventions.


Onboarding Data Support:


	Prepare merchant accounts ahead of onboarding by populating required product, inventory, and configuration data within agreed timelines.
	Review merchant - submitted data templates for errors or missing fields and follow up to resolve gaps before entry.
	Support the setup of catalogue structures, tax configurations, and payment settings as directed by the Onboarding team.


Data Validation & Quality Assurance:


	Conduct checks to identify and correct errors, duplicates, or outdated records.
	Cross-reference data across spreadsheets, CRM, and POS backend to ensure consistency.
	Flag and document data anomalies, routing them to the appropriate team for resolution.


Process & Documentation:


	Maintain accurate records of data entry activities, import logs, and correction history in the CRM.
	Document common errors and resolutions to build a shared knowledge base and reduce repeat mistakes.
	Identify recurring workflow bottlenecks and recommend improvements to the Operations lead.


Cross-Functional Collaboration:


	Fulfil ad-hoc data requests from Onboarding Specialists, Account Managers, and Support teams within SLA windows.
	Coordinate with internal teams to gather missing customer data without delaying onboarding timelines.


Qualifications


	1 - 3 years in data entry, data operations, or a similar role — preferably in SaaS, retail tech, or fintech.
	Exceptional attention to detail with a track record of high accuracy across large data volumes.
	Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets (data cleaning, VLOOKUP / XLOOKUP, basic formulas).
	Familiarity with CRM platforms or POS / back-office SaaS tools.
	Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.


Preferred:


	Experience with bulk CSV imports, data migration, or catalogue management in a SaaS context.
	Exposure to retail operations, inventory systems, or point - of - sale platforms.
	Experience supporting an onboarding, implementation, or customer success team.
	The candidate should be based in Edo State - Oredo and Ikpoba Okha.


About You:


	You're obsessively detail - orientated and take genuine pride in clean, accurate data.
	You're process - driven but proactive; you follow workflows and flag problems before they escalate.
	You're a team player who understands that your work sits at the heart of the customer journey.
	You're calm under pressure and can handle high volumes without cutting corners.
	You're tech - savvy and always looking for smarter, faster ways to work.


What Success Looks Like:


	99%+ data entry accuracy across merchant account builds and catalogue uploads.
	Zero go - live delays attributable to data readiness.
	All ad-hoc data requests fulfilled within defined SLA windows
	Open task backlog kept below 5% at any given time.
	Achieve >4.5+ average rating score from Onboarding Specialists and Account Managers on data quality and turnaround.


What we can offer you


	Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all voices are heard, and we look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
	Learning: We have a learning - and development - focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing and training.
	Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, plus other benefits.


What to expect in the hiring process


	A preliminary phone call with the recruiter.
	An interview with the hiring team.
	An interview with a member of our executive team.

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "JobPosting",
  "title": "Arts Project Manager",
  "description": "The British Council is the UK&rsquo;s international organisation for cultural relations and educational opportunities. We create friendly knowledge and understanding between the people of the UK and other countries. We do this by making a positive contribution to the UK and the countries we work with &ndash; changing lives by creating opportunities, building connections and engendering trust.
&nbsp;
We work with over 100 countries across the world in the fields of arts and culture, English language, education and civil society. Each year we reach over 20 million people face-to-face and more than 500 million people online, via broadcasts and publications. Founded in 1934, we are a UK charity governed by Royal Charter and a UK public body.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

Job Position: Arts Project Manager

Job Location: Nigeria

Role Context - About The Team


	Supports the delivery of the country Arts portfolio by managing the day-to-day coordination, logistics, procurement, compliance and reporting for assigned projects across creative economy, cultural exchange, capacity-building, grants and client-funded programmes.&nbsp;
	Works under the direction of the Arts Programme Manager to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget and to British Council quality, safeguarding and impact standards.


Role purpose &ndash; The job


	Cultural Engagement (CE) is one of two global strategic departments within the British Council. It brings together our work in Arts, Education, English &amp; School Education and research. With a workforce of approximately 1,000 globally and an income in 2024/25 of &pound;200 million, CE delivers impact through research and insight, sector engagement, policy dialogue and a mixed portfolio of commercial and Grant and Partnership Funded (GPF) work globally.
	Nigeria&rsquo;s creative industries continue to thrive, supported by the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy and the &lsquo;Destination 2030: Nigeria Everywhere&rsquo; initiative. Nollywood is the second largest film industry in the world and Afrobeats is the fifth most popular music genre globally. In February 2025, the British Council and the Federal Ministry entered into a Memorandum of Understanding to promote the creative arts, skills and connections amongst young people in the UK and Nigeria.
	Nigeria is a Top 12 priority country in the region and the British Council&rsquo;s largest operation in sub-Saharan Africa, with offices in Port Harcourt, Kano, Abuja and Lagos. The March 2026 Nigerian State Visit to the UK has elevated the bilateral relationship and created strong political momentum for cultural collaboration. Building on the success of the 2015/16 UK/Nigeria Arts Season, the British Council will host a second UK&ndash;Nigeria Season of Culture in 2028.
	Our Arts and Culture programme works across three broad areas: Creative Growth (unlocking inclusive and sustainable economic growth through research, advocacy, sector development and showcase programmes), Art in Action (building connections between UK and international artists and creative organisations), and Arts Core Offer (an inclusive portfolio of artist-led local content shared on our global platform).
	In 2026/27, Nigeria is delivering six interconnected programmes spanning film, visual arts, music, literature and creative hubs research, with each programme also feeding the Season of Culture 2028.
	The post holder will report to the Arts Programme Manager and will hold operational responsibility for project delivery across this portfolio, working closely with in-country delivery partners, suppliers and HMG stakeholders.&nbsp;
	The role is based in Lagos and is central to ensuring that every project meets British Council quality, compliance and impact standards.


Key Responsibilities
Project coordination and delivery:


	Coordinates the delivery of assigned arts projects, grants and cultural initiatives against agreed plans and milestones.
	Maintains delivery plans, tracks risks and issues, and monitors progress against agreed outcomes.
	Ensures compliance with safeguarding, health and safety, data protection and grant management requirements throughout the project lifecycle.


Procurement and contract management:


	Manages procurement and contracting processes for consultants, creative practitioners, delivery partners and suppliers on assigned projects.
	Ensures value for money and compliance with British Council procurement policies.
	Tracks contract performance and escalates issues to the Arts Programme Manager.


Financial management:


	Tracks project budgets and expenditure, processes procurement-to-payment workflows, and flags financial risks and variances to the Arts Programme Manager.
	Contributes to accurate reporting for internal stakeholders, funders and partners.
	Ensures adherence to British Council financial controls, audit requirements and donor regulations.


Monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting:


	Collates reporting from delivery partners, grant recipients, consultants and suppliers.
	Supports timely monitoring, evaluation, learning and impact reporting to meet organisational and donor requirements. Maintains project documentation and knowledge management systems.


Stakeholder and partner relationships:


	Builds and maintains working relationships with artists, creative practitioners, delivery partners, suppliers and other stakeholders to support programme impact and the UK&rsquo;s cultural relations objectives.
	Works collaboratively across internal teams and external networks to support high-quality project delivery.


Business development support:


	Supports business development by researching partnership opportunities, drafting sections of funding proposals, preparing budgets and costings, and contributing operational input to strategic planning for the Arts portfolio.


Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:


	Actively promotes inclusive, anti-racist and accessible approaches to programme design and delivery, ensuring meaningful participation of women, young people, persons with disabilities and underrepresented communities. Champions safeguarding, wellbeing, environmental sustainability and inclusive cultural participation across all programmes.


Requirements of the role
Minimum/essential:


	Bachelor&rsquo;s Degree or equivalent professional experience.
	Minimum of two years of experience managing arts, cultural, creative economy or development programmes from inception through completion.
	Demonstrated understanding of project management methodologies and project lifecycles.
	Experience managing programme budgets, financial reporting, forecasting and expenditure.
	Experience managing grants, procurement, contracts, suppliers and delivery partners.
	Experience building and managing relationships with multiple stakeholders, including government, creative sector organisations, donors and international partners.
	Experience managing monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting processes.
	Knowledge of safeguarding, procurement, compliance and risk management requirements.
	Experience using digital technologies and online collaboration tools to deliver programmes.
	Strong communication, planning, organisational and stakeholder management skills.


Desirable:


	Professional Project Management qualification (e.g. APMG PMD Pro, PRINCE2, PMP, Agile).
	Experience working within the arts, creative industries, cultural relations or international development sectors.
	Knowledge of Nigeria&rsquo;s creative economy and cultural sector.
	Experience developing funding proposals, business cases and partnership agreements.
	Experience managing international cultural exchange programmes and artist mobility initiatives.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

Job Position: Arts Project Manager

Job Location: Nigeria

Role Context - About The Team


	Supports the delivery of the country Arts portfolio by managing the day-to-day coordination, logistics, procurement, compliance and reporting for assigned projects across creative economy, cultural exchange, capacity-building, grants and client-funded programmes. 
	Works under the direction of the Arts Programme Manager to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget and to British Council quality, safeguarding and impact standards.


Role purpose – The job


	Cultural Engagement (CE) is one of two global strategic departments within the British Council. It brings together our work in Arts, Education, English & School Education and research. With a workforce of approximately 1,000 globally and an income in 2024/25 of £200 million, CE delivers impact through research and insight, sector engagement, policy dialogue and a mixed portfolio of commercial and Grant and Partnership Funded (GPF) work globally.
	Nigeria’s creative industries continue to thrive, supported by the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy and the ‘Destination 2030: Nigeria Everywhere’ initiative. Nollywood is the second largest film industry in the world and Afrobeats is the fifth most popular music genre globally. In February 2025, the British Council and the Federal Ministry entered into a Memorandum of Understanding to promote the creative arts, skills and connections amongst young people in the UK and Nigeria.
	Nigeria is a Top 12 priority country in the region and the British Council’s largest operation in sub-Saharan Africa, with offices in Port Harcourt, Kano, Abuja and Lagos. The March 2026 Nigerian State Visit to the UK has elevated the bilateral relationship and created strong political momentum for cultural collaboration. Building on the success of the 2015/16 UK/Nigeria Arts Season, the British Council will host a second UK–Nigeria Season of Culture in 2028.
	Our Arts and Culture programme works across three broad areas: Creative Growth (unlocking inclusive and sustainable economic growth through research, advocacy, sector development and showcase programmes), Art in Action (building connections between UK and international artists and creative organisations), and Arts Core Offer (an inclusive portfolio of artist-led local content shared on our global platform).
	In 2026/27, Nigeria is delivering six interconnected programmes spanning film, visual arts, music, literature and creative hubs research, with each programme also feeding the Season of Culture 2028.
	The post holder will report to the Arts Programme Manager and will hold operational responsibility for project delivery across this portfolio, working closely with in-country delivery partners, suppliers and HMG stakeholders. 
	The role is based in Lagos and is central to ensuring that every project meets British Council quality, compliance and impact standards.


Key Responsibilities
Project coordination and delivery:


	Coordinates the delivery of assigned arts projects, grants and cultural initiatives against agreed plans and milestones.
	Maintains delivery plans, tracks risks and issues, and monitors progress against agreed outcomes.
	Ensures compliance with safeguarding, health and safety, data protection and grant management requirements throughout the project lifecycle.


Procurement and contract management:


	Manages procurement and contracting processes for consultants, creative practitioners, delivery partners and suppliers on assigned projects.
	Ensures value for money and compliance with British Council procurement policies.
	Tracks contract performance and escalates issues to the Arts Programme Manager.


Financial management:


	Tracks project budgets and expenditure, processes procurement-to-payment workflows, and flags financial risks and variances to the Arts Programme Manager.
	Contributes to accurate reporting for internal stakeholders, funders and partners.
	Ensures adherence to British Council financial controls, audit requirements and donor regulations.


Monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting:


	Collates reporting from delivery partners, grant recipients, consultants and suppliers.
	Supports timely monitoring, evaluation, learning and impact reporting to meet organisational and donor requirements. Maintains project documentation and knowledge management systems.


Stakeholder and partner relationships:


	Builds and maintains working relationships with artists, creative practitioners, delivery partners, suppliers and other stakeholders to support programme impact and the UK’s cultural relations objectives.
	Works collaboratively across internal teams and external networks to support high-quality project delivery.


Business development support:


	Supports business development by researching partnership opportunities, drafting sections of funding proposals, preparing budgets and costings, and contributing operational input to strategic planning for the Arts portfolio.


Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:


	Actively promotes inclusive, anti-racist and accessible approaches to programme design and delivery, ensuring meaningful participation of women, young people, persons with disabilities and underrepresented communities. Champions safeguarding, wellbeing, environmental sustainability and inclusive cultural participation across all programmes.


Requirements of the role
Minimum/essential:


	Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent professional experience.
	Minimum of two years of experience managing arts, cultural, creative economy or development programmes from inception through completion.
	Demonstrated understanding of project management methodologies and project lifecycles.
	Experience managing programme budgets, financial reporting, forecasting and expenditure.
	Experience managing grants, procurement, contracts, suppliers and delivery partners.
	Experience building and managing relationships with multiple stakeholders, including government, creative sector organisations, donors and international partners.
	Experience managing monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting processes.
	Knowledge of safeguarding, procurement, compliance and risk management requirements.
	Experience using digital technologies and online collaboration tools to deliver programmes.
	Strong communication, planning, organisational and stakeholder management skills.


Desirable:


	Professional Project Management qualification (e.g. APMG PMD Pro, PRINCE2, PMP, Agile).
	Experience working within the arts, creative industries, cultural relations or international development sectors.
	Knowledge of Nigeria’s creative economy and cultural sector.
	Experience developing funding proposals, business cases and partnership agreements.
	Experience managing international cultural exchange programmes and artist mobility initiatives.
